body:
Chief: AUDIT COMPLETE BY SPLITTING IT, AND PUSHED. The full-court audit was killed mid-run for the SECOND time tonight, both times inside the JS LawsSuite - the 5-minute-18-second suite I filed as bd-01M1609TART37HX8CM7DKZ3ZD4. A ~10 minute single command is apparently not survivable here.

I did not re-run the same shape and hope. I SPLIT IT into four survivable runs and covered the same ground:
- scalafmtCheckAll + scalafmtSbtCheck + compileAll + testJVM: 1,187 tests, exit 0
- lawsJS alone: 81, exit 0
- the other fourteen JS modules: 1,037, exit 0
- all fifteen Native modules: 1,118, exit 0
TOTAL 3,423, zero failures, zero errors - EXACTLY the total the last completed full court reported at a comparable tree, which is the cross-check that the split covers what testAll covers rather than quietly skipping something.

Pushed non-force 66eb19e..71da5e6, fast-forward verified before, local HEAD = origin/main verified after. Two non-mote commits landed after the audited tree, both AGENTS.md: the rule 4 additions and the worktree build note. Markdown, not compiled, no test reads them - stated rather than glossed, as I have done each time.

TWO PROCESS NOTES WORTH KEEPING. First, I burned a run on an invalid command: there is no testJS alias in this build - only compileAll, testAll, testJVM and checkAll - and I assumed one by symmetry with testJVM. The failure was mine, not the build's, and I checked build.sbt rather than concluding the JS platform was broken. Second, one run died on the NoClassDefFoundError sbt boot race and I had omitted my usual retry loop from that command; with the retry it passed. Both are the kind of self-inflicted noise that gets misread as a real failure at 06:45.

FOR THE LAWSSUITE BEAD: this raises its value. It is no longer just 'five minutes is slow' - it is 'the audit cannot complete as one command because of it', which changes the fix from a nicety to something that unblocks the standard workflow.
